sources.entry: dataclasses - (Python standard library) Adds generated special methods such as init() and repr() to your classes.

summary.name: dataclasses
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module providing the @dataclass decorator, which auto-generates special methods such as __init__() and __repr__() for classes based on type-annotated fields.
use_cases: Reduce boilerplate when writing simple data-holding classes
Create immutable value objects with frozen=True
Convert nested objects to dicts or tuples for serialization
Set default values and mutable defaults for class fields
Dynamically create classes from field specifications with make_dataclass
summary.what_it_does: The @dataclass decorator inspects a class for fields defined as type-annotated class variables and adds generated methods such as __init__(), __repr__(), __eq__(), and optionally ordering and hash methods. Options like frozen, order, slots, kw_only and match_args control the generated code. The field() function sets per-field defaults, default factories, and repr, compare, and hash behavior. Helper functions include fields(), asdict(), astuple(), replace(), is_dataclass() and make_dataclass(). Support for __post_init__() and InitVar pseudo-fields allows computed or init-only values.
notable: Generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ from PEP 526 type annotations, added in Python 3.7
frozen=True emulates immutable instances; slots=True generates __slots__ (3.10+)
Helpers asdict(), astuple(), replace() and make_dataclass() for conversion and dynamic creation
Listed in awesome-python under Built-in Classes Enhancement
caveats: Frozen instances are only emulated, not truly immutable; frozen=True adds a small performance cost
slots=True raises TypeError if base class __init_subclass__ is passed parameters (gh-91126)
Some features require newer Python versions (match_args and kw_only from 3.10, weakref_slot from 3.11)
